triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The three rules applying the 12.5% forced-labor 301 duty to products of Brazil under HTS 9903.05.27 started 2026-07-23, one day before the notice makes the additional duty applicable to entries on or after July 24, 2026, so 07-23 entries were charged a duty the source had not yet imposed.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 4, applied to three rules (heading predicate plus the general and special duty-rate overlays); the imported 12.5% rate parameter lives in forced-labor-presidential-action and was not changed. FR 2026-15181 DATES verified through the pinned corpus (see index 4). Companion test unchanged; manifest re-signed with manual_exception "repair".
triage.verifier_justification: The diff is exclusively three `effective_from` edits, one per rule, moving the single version window of the 9903.05.27 forced-labor Brazil overlay from 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-24, with formulas, rates, inputs, outputs, proof atoms, and scope untouched — a change to encoded meaning (the version window), not provenance. I read the cited notice through the pinned corpus release (us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-07-28/2026-15181, resolved text sha e1f… for the HTS heading and 2fe7… for the notice): its DATES paragraph reads "The additional rates of duty are applicable with respect to products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026", so the pre-fix window started the +12.5% duty one day before the source imposed it. My refutation attempts failed: the module's own cited source (HTS 9903.05.27) carries no date at all, so 07-23 had no grounding in it — the July 23 date belongs to the presidential memorandum encoded in a different module (forced-labor-presidential-action.yaml), which correctly keeps effective_from '2026-07-23' and is unchanged here. Nothing about the change is a comparison-strictness fix, an added clause, or new coverage, so no other kind fits better than wrong_period_or_effective_date.
triage.verifier_notes: Strongest (but insufficient) counterargument for a reviewer: the PR body lists the old state as a deliberate judgment call — "Forced-labor 301 component gated at ≥ 2026-07-24 per FR 2026-15181 DATES, although heading modules carry effective_from 2026-07-23" — and the composition already gated the component at ≥ 2026-07-24, so the wrong module window was masked at the composed-program level and no companion test changed (all three cases in forced-labor-brazil-9903-05-27.test.yaml are dated 2026-08-01). It is still a real fidelity defect: the module is an independently evaluable artifact whose 2026-07-23 evaluation would have returned general/special rates inflated by 12.5 points, and the repair commit treats it as a correction ("Forced-labor 301 headings gate entries on/after 2026-07-24 per FR 2026-15181 DATES (was 2026-07-23)"), re-signing the manifest with manual_exception "repair". Two notes for corpus hygiene: (1) the same 07-23 → 07-24 shift is applied across the sibling forced-labor heading modules in this commit (module_files 4, 6, 7, 8), so if the corpus dedupes near-identical defects, this case is one of five instances of the same fix — keep one or mark the family; (2) the DATES paragraph also carries an in-transit carve-out ("goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, and entered … before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026, shall not be subject to such additional duty") that the module still does not encode after the fix — a candidate unrepresented_clause defect, but not the one this commit repairs, so it should not be folded into this case.
